  "entityC2": {
    "design_critique": "1) The early-failure evidence is still unaddressed. Across 60 trials and five designs, every run ended off track with 1 to 2 line-loss events, max_error at 0.061 to 0.067, and progress of 0.04 to 0.17. Those outcomes held across kp 2.5 to 5, kd 0.02 to 0.1, sensor spans of 0.03 to 0.04 m, sensor sizes of 0.012 and 0.016, and base_speed 1.5 to 1.7. The revision changes sensor count, spacing, footprint and weights again, but it does not test the fixed cause the Optimizer's own rationale names. A progress of about 0.1 on a 4 to 5 m course means the robot leaves the line within about 0.5 m. Sensor geometry and gain changes are unlikely to alter an early divergence that they have not altered in any of the five designs so far.

2) The 2 percent left/right motor mismatch is not corrected. With ki 0, the steady signal offset is about mismatch/kp. At kp 4.5 this is slightly smaller than at kp 5, so the bias is not new, but it is still uncorrected, and it pushes the robot toward one edge on a long course. The rationale calls ki 0 'inert', which is true for the clamp magnitude but ignores this bias.

3) Saturation sits in the failure zone. Outer-wheel saturation begins near |signal| 0.65 at base_pwm 3071 and kp 4.5. The off-track limit is 0.06 m, and the outer sensors (weights plus or minus 1) read the largest signal when the robot is already far off the centre line. So the saturated regime is reached exactly when the robot is near the boundary. The design is therefore not free of steering loss at the moment it matters, even though the rationale calls this a known limit, not a failure.

4) Seven narrow sensors divide by the sum of readings. Near the tape edge the sum is small, and the normalised signal becomes noise-sensitive there. kd 0.1 gives about 0.2 turn units for a 0.02 step, but that calculation assumes a clean reading. The design adds sensors without measuring the noise level, so the kd margin is unverified.

5) The speed is still a dimensionless demand. base_speed 1.5 gives base_pwm 3071, about 75 percent of full drive. Battery sag, rolling resistance and slip all reduce real speed, so the robot may not average the 1.5 m/s needed to finish within 3 s. The 500-point completion term is at risk, and nothing in the design measures this.

6) The 7-sensor array with 0.01 m spacing and 0.012 footprints leaves 2 mm gaps, so a tape edge can still fall between sensors. The design gives up the overlap the round-1 critique favoured, without saying why.",
    "rationale_critique": "1) The 'best raced geometry' claim is wrong on the lookahead. The rationale says y = 0.06 is a moderate increase over the raced 0.04 m. But iteration 0, which scored best at 39.85, used y = 0.06, and 0.04 was used only in iterations 1 and 2. The rationale should say that this geometry was already raced and did not change the outcome.

2) The claim that the 5-sensor version 'has already shown a flat score' is an overreach. Flat scores show that the 5-sensor variants did not differ, not that the 5-sensor layout is worse or better. Replacing it with an untested 7-sensor layout is a hypothesis, and the rationale does not say how it would detect that the change is harmful.

3) The rationale says the failure 'may be set early in the course' and that the next iteration should look for a fixed early divergence. But the observation request contains only aggregate metrics and no time series, so this race cannot locate the divergence. The plan to find it is not carried by the test as written.

4) The saturation section calls the outer-wheel limit a 'known limit, not a failure of the design'. Saturation at |signal| 0.65 is the regime near the 0.06 m boundary, so the rationale should say whether that is acceptable, not dismiss it.

5) The speed claim links base_speed 1.5 to the 1.5 m/s ground speed needed to finish. base_speed is dimensionless, so the link is asserted, not derived. The rationale admits the speed is unmeasured, but it still uses 1.5 as the nearest value that meets the requirement.

6) Several falsifiable targets are weak. max_error below 0.06 is the off-track boundary itself, so a pass only means not failing. steering_oscillation below 0.15 has no mechanism behind it, and the raced baseline is 0.16 to 0.18. progress above 0.5 is a reasonable test, but the rationale gives no fallback if it fails.

7) The rationale does not say which single change to revert first if the race fails. Several variables change at once (sensor count, spacing, footprint, weights, kp, kd, base_speed), so the attribution goal stated in earlier rounds is not met."
